rv.q: For all that, it's still an Ayckbourn, which means you will laugh and you will be left with much to ponder.
Ayckbourn is full of ideas, but in The Trial of Romeo Oscar they seem somewhat undigested.
If it feels indulgent and piggybacks on Shakespeare to convey the beauty and heartbreak of the human condition, the production finds a transcendent quality in these moments.

cn.t: Ayckbourn's 92nd play ventures into sci-fi territory with mixed results, exploring humanity's future through an android murder trial that philosophizes about consciousness and art's enduring power.
